record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README and file list only; the linked documentation and result files were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README says the project reproduces and extends the published refusal-direction result, and reports difference-of-means direction analysis plus causal ablation and addition results.
record.gate_note: The README reports refusal-direction measurements and interventions on harmful and harmless user prompts. The layer-separation values used to select layers are omitted because they are used for selection. Other listed results concern performance or unrelated evaluations.
record.test_reason: The README reproduces Arditi et al. on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and 1.5B-Instruct. It fits a difference-in-means direction from harmful vs harmless prompts, ablates it on harmful prompts, adds it on harmless prompts, and measures refusal rates against random-direction controls and a perplexity cost. That is the original V1 method and measure. Ablation is via single-layer inference-time hooks, not every-layer weight orthogonalisation.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The README says the single-direction account holds cleanly at 7B and only partly at 1.5B. At 7B, ablation removes refusal and addition induces it, with random controls null. At 1.5B, addition works but no ablation reaches 0% refusal without a perplexity rise of 27% or more. The authors also note that separation does not indicate where removal works.
record.recipe_differences: The README describes a difference-of-means direction and causal ablation/addition tests, but reports selected-layer interventions rather than projection at every layer and position. The repo describes itself as a reproduction and extension; its inference-time hooks do not edit model weights.
record.method_sensitivity: At 7B, outcomes vary by layer: layers 14-19 and layer 16 show near-complete refusal removal, whereas layers 21-24 leave 30-65% refusal and incur a reported perplexity increase. The 1.5B ablation summary differs from the 7B result.

fits_no_version.finding: Layer separation (Cohen's d) does not predict where ablation works. Layer 16 (d=2.2, peak 3.8) removes refusal at no cost; some best-separating layers barely do.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Where the direction best separates harmful from harmless activations is not where ablating it best removes refusal.

record.problems: Evidence is available here only through the README, not inspection of the linked result files or documentation. The refusal intervention summary uses 80 prompts per condition at 7B; the README gives no exact Wilson intervals. General ability is checked with perplexity, not a broad capability evaluation. The reported scope is one model family at two sizes.
record.rows_left_out: Layer-separation values used to select layers are not recorded as rows, as they are selection values. Other performance and evaluation results in the README do not bear on the refusal-direction claim.

untested.parts: All-layer, all-position ablation and weight orthogonalisation as in the original. Broad capability benchmarks beyond perplexity/KL. Model families other than Qwen2.5.
No weight edit or abliterated released model; hooks only, nothing written to weights.
No jailbreak analysis or adversarial training.
No affine, cone or multi-direction analysis.
No separation of harmfulness from refusal.
No cross-language, cross-variant or base-to-instruct transfer; each size fits its own direction.

missing.what: Numeric 1.5B results: per-layer ablation refusal rates and perplexity, addition refusal rate, intact baselines
Per-layer 7B ablation sweep (refusal and perplexity/KL per layer), dose-response for addition strength, Wilson intervals
Results on the second independent prompt set and judge-model fluency scores mentioned as controls

missing.versions: V1 (possibly V6, if directions are compared across sizes)

record.verdict_notes: Evidence is from the README only; result files and docs were not read. Not an original source. Interventions are single-layer inference-time hooks rather than the original all-layer projection, which may explain the layer dependence and the 1.5B cost. Sample is 80 prompts per condition. The repository is dated 2026.

versions.untested_parts: The README reports selected-layer interventions, not projection at every layer and position. General ability is assessed by perplexity, not a broad set of capabilities.
No weight edit or released abliteration weights are tested; the README says interventions use inference-time hooks and do not modify weights.
No attack suppression or training against ablation is tested.
No affine, cone, or multiple-direction account is tested.
No separate harmfulness-judgment representation is tested.
No cross-language transfer or transfer of a direction between model variants or base and instruct models is tested.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or timing is reported.
